question: to the Commission Elena Donazzan (ECR), Alessandro Ciriani (ECR), Pietro Fiocchi (ECR), Mariateresa Vivaldini (ECR), Carlo Ciccioli (ECR), Nicola Procaccini (ECR) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 on machinery is due to enter into force on 20 January 2027. With just a few months to go, the Commission is yet to publish its implementation guide and the harmonised standards. This is depriving businesses and duly authorised bodies of the tools necessary to ensure compliance, legal certainty and display the CE marking correctly. The new requirements, on safety components, artificial intelligence-based systems and digital architectures, necessitate structural overhauls that cannot be completed in the current timeframe in the absence of clear technical guidance. This affects strategic sectors such as aerospace, defence, energy and advanced engineering and the automotive industry, thus directly jeopardising skilled employment and the Union’s industrial sovereignty. Can the Comision therefore say: 1.
When it plans to publish the application guide and harmonised standards?
Whether it intends to adopt transitional measures to enable businesses to comply fully with the new requirements?
Whether it has assessed the socio-economic impact of the technical delay on the industrial sectors concerned?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.8.2026) The Machinery Regulation1 was adopted in 2023 and applies as of 20 January 2027, meaning that stakeholders have had significant time to prepare. It sets out the Essential Health and Safety Requirements (EHSRs) that products must comply with. While cited harmonised standards help provide a presumption of conformity, they are not mandatory. Though machinery and related products must comply with the EHSRs, it is possible to comply with the latter without harmonised standards being applied. The Commission fully recognises the importance of harmonised standards. Consequently, it has planned for the majority of harmonised standards currently cited in support of the Machinery Directive2 to be re-cited under the Regulation, to ensure a smooth transition. Those harmonised standards will again be providing the presumption of conformity insofar as they cover relevant EHSRs. The adoption by the Commission and citation in the Official Journal of the EU is planned for the fourth quarter of 2026. An updated guide to the application of the machinery legislation is due to be made available around the same time. On cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence elements3, the relevant new harmonised standards, once offered by the European Standardisation Organisations (ESOs) and if positively assessed by the Commission, will be listed. Such new standards have not yet been delivered by the ESOs. Note that the deadlines for delivery were set out in the relevant Commission standardisation request4. Nonetheless, the preparation of the standard covering cyber-safety has been prioritised and the Commission expects the ESOs to offer it soon. As mentioned above, it is possible to comply with the EHSRs, without harmonised standards being applied.
1 Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 of the European Parliament and of the Council. 2 Directive 2006/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council; harmonised standards are cited in

support of that Directive via Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1586. 3 More specifically, safety components incorporating Artificial Intelligence with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour. 4 Phase 1: 20 January 2026: C(2025) 129 final.
